brief.headline: Signed for by D REYES, 3DS-authenticated, buyer praised it in chat — fight the unauthorized chargeback
brief.summary: The cardholder filed an unauthorized-transaction chargeback (code 1040) for a $420 briefcase. The records show it was authorized and received: 3-D Secure authenticated, AVS/CVV matched, checkout came from the buyer's known device and Columbus IP, UPS got a signature from D REYES at the transaction address, and the buyer messaged the store the next day saying the briefcase "arrived, it's beautiful." Seller Protection checks show it is likely eligible. PayPal is already reviewing, so the case goes in through provide_supporting_info.

reasoning.point: Seller Protection is likely eligible: PayPal flags the payment as eligible for unauthorized claims, the item shipped to the transaction address with verifiable UPS tracking, and it shipped 1 day after payment.
UPS 2nd Day Air with signature required delivered on 2026-09-28 to 481 Oak Park Ave, Columbus OH 43215, signed by D REYES. This matches the transaction shipping and billing address.

Payment authentication was strong: 3-D Secure AUTHENTICATED, AVS Y, CVV M. The checkout IP was in Columbus, 4 km from the shipping address, on a device first seen 2026-02-02. The email is 3,400 days old.
After delivery, the buyer confirmed receipt in chat on 2026-09-29: 'Briefcase arrived, it's beautiful' and asked about the lock code.
This is an established customer: 3 orders since Feb 2026 (KA-9466, KA-9603), $664 lifetime value, no prior disputes.
Status is UNDER_REVIEW and only provide_supporting_info is open to the seller. Proof of fulfillment is already on file, so the response adds the authentication and post-purchase evidence.

risks: Card-network chargebacks are decided by the issuer, so Seller Protection may not fully apply to an external chargeback. The issuer could still side with the cardholder.
The cardholder may argue a household member placed the order. The signature and chat show the goods reached and were used by the account holder's household, but this is not airtight.
There is no delivery photo. The proof rests on the UPS signature and tracking.

brief.headline: Wallet returned to sender as undeliverable and never refunded: accept the $68 chargeback
brief.summary: Jordan Kim's $68 Bifold Wallet (KA-10511) shipped by USPS on Sept 23. On Sept 28 USPS marked it "Undeliverable as addressed — no such number" and returned it to Kora Atelier on Oct 6. The buyer emailed on Oct 8 asking where it was, no refund was issued, and they then filed a card chargeback for item not received. The buyer never received the item and the merchant has it back, so this can't be won. Accept the claim and offer to reship once the buyer confirms their address.

reasoning.point: USPS tracking shows the parcel was never delivered. It was marked undeliverable (no such number) in Portland on Sept 28 and delivered back to the sender in Brooklyn on Oct 6.
No refund has been issued on the order, so we cannot provide PROOF_OF_REFUND, and PROOF_OF_FULFILLMENT would only show a return to sender.
Seller Protection does not apply: item-not-received chargebacks filed with the card issuer are excluded. The playbook also says to refund, not fight, when an item is returned to sender.

The buyer asked about the parcel on Oct 8, two days after it came back, and the record shows no reply. This is a first-time customer with no prior disputes, so it looks like a real failed delivery, not abuse.
The address problem (possibly a typo by the buyer at checkout) doesn't change the outcome. The merchant has the wallet back, so it can be restocked and the only loss is shipping.

risks: Accepting the claim may not reverse the chargeback fee. Fighting would add costs and almost certainly lose.
If the buyer also gets a refund some other way, make sure no second refund is issued outside this chargeback.

brief.headline: Return received Oct 16, no refund issued yet — accept the $180 chargeback, don't fight
brief.summary: Priya Patel returned the Weekend Clutch on a prepaid UPS label we sent her. UPS shows it delivered to the studio on Oct 16, signed by K. Nair. The order shows no refund, so her card issuer opened a "credit not processed" chargeback on Oct 20. We have no proof of refund, so this can't be won. Accepting the $180 claim refunds a loyal 5-order customer and avoids paying her twice.

reasoning.point: The buyer asked to return the item on Oct 10, within 30 days of the Sep 19 delivery. The merchant agreed, sent a prepaid label and promised a refund within 3 business days of the return arriving.
UPS return tracking shows the parcel delivered to Kora Atelier on 2026-10-16, received by K. NAIR.
The order record shows no refunds. The buyer followed up on Oct 18 and got no reply. The chargeback was filed on Oct 20.

PayPal wants PROOF_OF_REFUND for a credit-not-processed claim, and we can't provide it. The 3-business-day window runs to about Oct 21, so the buyer filed slightly early. Even so, the merchant owes this refund, and fighting would only add fees and lose the customer.
This is a good long-term customer: 5 orders, $905 lifetime value and no earlier disputes.

risks: Do not also refund the capture by hand in PayPal or the shop. That would pay the buyer twice on top of the chargeback.
Nobody has inspected the returned clutch yet (no QC photo). If it comes back damaged or used, that is a separate matter and does not change this chargeback.
